title: Angle hold: experimental challenge failure
instructions: An honest-style scripted stand-in (not a human) holds the doorway's left frame from across the room, as a player waiting for a push would. A near-still probe rests in the chamber behind that frame. Nobody is following anything.

card.what_this_tests: The known weakness of the time-on-body bar: ordinary angle holding over a probe that happens to rest behind the held angle.
card.player_can_know: No. And the player is not responding to anything: the aim never moves.
card.server_knows: Vision absent and audio absent for the body at every moment; the aim cone held the body because the chamber is behind the frame.
card.expected_fpsdet_behavior: Challenge followed, decision review: the same evidence as the follower. EXPERIMENTAL, NOT PRODUCTION QUALIFIED. Geometric alignment is not the same thing as responding to hidden information.
card.invalid_if: The holder's aim moves with the body, which would make it a follower. Here the body is near-still and the aim is still.

caveats: Challenge reviews are experimental and not production-qualified. The bar counts time on the body, not intent.
This failure is preserved on purpose: it is why the consented human pilot exists and why occluded_motion_replay/3 asks whether the aim turns with secret turns instead.
actor: HONEST-STYLE SCRIPTED STAND-IN (holds an angle) · NOT A HUMAN
